newsitem.title: GREECE: HSBC James Capel says Michaniki a buy.
newsitem.headline: HSBC James Capel says Michaniki a buy.

text.p: HSBC James Capel upgraded Greek construction firm Michaniki to a buy, citing superior earnings growth and its strategy to diversify out of general turnkey construction and out of Greece.

Michaniki's operating revenues from build-operate-tranfer (BOT) projects have been overlooked and its three-year long underperformance was set to reverse, HSBC James Capel said in its buy recommendation dated March 13.

"The stock is trading at discounts to all sector and market multiples when, in fact, it has superior earnings growth. We believe this is an aberration that should clear once investors start to appreciate the excellent prospects," said analyst John Embiricos.
Michaniki has been at the vanguard of Greece's construction sector, undertaking self-financed concession projects, working with foreign companies and expanding outside Greece.
It has also diversified into the related businesses of light engineering, steel pipe manufacture and timber section production.
While turnkey construction projects within Greece are the most important source of revenues at the moment, their relative importance will gradually give way to other activities.

"Over the next three to five years competition can only increase, EU funding of infrastructure projects diminish and local profit margins fall. The two key elements of strategy are to diversify out of general turnkey construction and out of Greece," the report said.
It forecast Michaniki's consolidated turnover will grow 29 percent this year to 35.1 billion drachmas and 26 percent in 1998 to 44.2 billion.
Net profit will grow 30 percent to 4.72 billion drachmas this year and reach 5.66 billion in 1998, it said.

"We regard Michaniki's steps toward expansion beyond Greek borders as extremely positive. Certainly there are risks attached to such ventures but these will be lower than staying within the confines of the local market," it said.
